results.condition:
I want you to build a first-person shooter at the level of the most recent Call of Duty games. It should be utterly perfect, visually beautiful, with every single thing done at AAA quality—from textures to physics to anything you could think of.

Fan out sub-agents and have sub-agents tackle each one individually so that the game is utterly perfect. You should /loop on each item and have a separate sub-agent check it visually to ensure it looks triple A. That separate sub-agent should be a really harsh critic, and if it doesn't look triple A, it should keep going.

Don't stop until each sub-agent is utterly wowed with the quality when compared with the actual Call of Duty game. It should literally compare them side by side blind and say which one looks better. Do this in ThreeJS. /loop until it's utterly perfect. Fan out sub-agents and ultracode.

Workflow requirements: use the oh-my-openagent project at https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent as requested. Deliver a concrete playable Three.js first-person shooter in the repository. Use the load-sketchfab-threejs skill to find a suitable downloadable GLB asset, preserve attribution, and verify geometry, materials, and animations. Use the gauntlet-loop iteration and visual-critic process, with browser-visible proof and tests where applicable. Keep iterating within the workflow and report evidence for what was actually completed.

Mandatory workflow skills: gauntlet-loop, load-sketchfab-threejs. Before implementing, read every listed skill's `SKILL.md` and follow its instructions for this request. If a listed skill applies to the requested feature or assets, you must use it; do not substitute a generic or procedural workaround when the skill provides the required workflow. For example, when `load-sketchfab-threejs` is listed, use it to obtain and integrate at least one suitable Sketchfab/GLB asset, preserve attribution, and verify that asset renders in the browser. If a listed skill genuinely does not apply, state why in the completion report.

Mandatory orchestration: before declaring the game complete, use OpenCode's `task` tool to launch separate child sessions for:

- builder: implement or improve the game feature;
- critic: independently inspect the current browser result against a concrete named reference and report the single biggest remaining gap;
- verifier: run browser checks and verify the gameplay loop.

Launch independent builder/critic work as parallel background subagents when supported. Wait for all child sessions, apply the critic's concrete finding through an implementation or remediation step, and run verification again afterward. Do not claim a critique loop ran unless the task tool returns distinct child session IDs and the critic produces a concrete finding. If the task tool is unavailable, stop and report the blocker instead of silently doing the work in one agent.

  This is a /loop request. Preserve the original goal above as the source of truth. Before the first completion and before every later iteration, use the task tool to ask for distinct parallel builder, critic, and verifier subagents. The critic must inspect the current browser-visible game/app against a concrete reference and return the single biggest gap; apply that finding, re-verify the gameplay loop, and only then declare the iteration complete. After each completion, publish the latest playable result by committing and pushing the project changes and updating the triggering issue, then immediately continue the same goal for the next improvement. Do not stop after publishing and do not create a second PR.
